<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="DjR" /></noinclude><section begin="par112"/>&c. (so {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=12}}), with a frequentative perfect consecutive. The perfect consecutive is very frequently used to announce future actions or events after simple expressions of time of any kind; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=34}} (after {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}} with the infinitive), cf. also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=6|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=23|hidebook=1}} (numerous frequentative perfects consecutive after the infinitive with a preposition; so {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=5}}, see above, ee); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=5}}; moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=26|hidebook=1}}; even after single disconnected words, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫רֶב וִֽידַעְתֶּם|translate=at even}} (when it becomes evening) ''then ye shall know''; cf. verse 7, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=27}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|pp}}
'''6.''' Finally there still remains a number of passages which cannot be classed with any of those hitherto mentioned. Of these, some are due to the influence of Aramaic modes of expression, while in others the text is evidently corrupt.<ref>Mayer Lambert, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxvi. 55, is probably right in pointing some of these forms as ''infin. abs.'' instead of ''perfects''.</ref> In a few instances we can do no more than merely call attention to the incorrectness of the expression. (We are not of course concerned here with the cases—usually occurring in dependent clauses—in which a 2nd pers. ''perf.'' with Wāw copulative is simply co-ordinate with what precedes, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=6}}, and probably {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=2}}.)

(''a'') The influence of the Aramaic construction of the perfect with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} as the narrative tense, instead of the Hebrew imperfect consecutive (cf. Kautzsch, {{GHGcite|title=Gramm. des Bibl.-Aram.}}, {{GHGpar|71|b}}), is certainly to be traced in ''Qoheleth'', and sporadically in other very late books,<ref>In the whole of ''Qoheleth'' the imperfect consecutive occurs only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=17|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=1.7|hidebook=1}}. Several of the perfects with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} can no doubt be explained as frequentatives, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=5|hidebook=1.9.11.13.15}}, 5:18, compared with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=6|verse=2|hidebook=1}}; but this is impossible in such passages as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=14|hidebook=1}} ff. In Ezra, Driver reckons only six examples of the historical perfect with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, in Nehemiah only six, and in Esther six or seven.</ref> perhaps also in a few passages in the hooks of Kings, which are open to the suspicion of being due to later interpolation; so probably {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=32}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהֶֽעֱמִידִ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} {{GHGheb|text=וראתה}}; 14:14 {{GHGheb|text=וְלָקַח}} (in the parallel passage, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=24}}, the word is wanting); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=וְנַשָׂא}}, &c.; verse 10 {{GHGheb|text=וְטִמֵּא}}, &c.; verse 12 {{GHGheb|text=וְהִשְׁלִיךְ}}, &c.; verse 15 {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׂרַף}}, &c.<ref>Stade in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} v. 291 ff. and in ''Ausgeäwhlte akad. Reden'', Giessen, 1899, p. 194 ff. and appendix p. 199, discusses, in connexion with {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=12|verse=12}}, a number of critically questionable perfects with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}. He considers that the whole section, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=4}} from {{GHGheb|text=וְנָשָׂא}} to verse 5 inclusive, is to be regarded as a gloss, since the continuation of an imperfect consecutive by means of a perfect with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} never occurs in pre-exilic documents, except in places where it is due to corruption of the original text. The theory of frequentative perfects consecutive (even immediately after imperfects consecutive), which has been supported above, under f and g, by a large number of examples, is quite inconsistent with the character of the action in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהִשְׁבִּית}}, verse 8 {{GHGheb|text=וְנָתָץ}}, and verse 14 {{GHGheb|text=וְשִׁבַּר}}.</ref> Cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=2}}, 7, 10.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|qq}}
(''b'') The text is certainly corrupt in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=6}} (read with the LXX and Vulgate<section end="par112"/><noinclude>
